start_here: Say to your AI: "Read my YouTube Watch Later, subscriptions and playlists for my kitchen channel into a private folder." It reads the tool's row, writes the request file with your cookies.txt and sort settings, runs read_channel.py on your computer and tells you the counts per channel.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope: here the row record:setting:sort-youtube-watch-later-into-playlists~person~<person> whose settings JSON names the channels to read and how each is sorted.

instructions: 1. Pour the example settings row into your own settings list (see pour), or make list:settings from it, and change the channel's slug, label and sign_in_as to your own.

2. Export your browser's YouTube login with tool:export-browser-login-cookies-for-yt-dlp, then check it: echo '{"cookies":"cookies.txt"}' | python3 -I tools/sort-youtube-watch-later-into-playlists/do-work/list_signed_in_accounts.py must say signed_in true.

3. Say the start_here sentence. Your AI reads this tool's row with tools:list, writes a request {cookies, settings_record, out_dir} and runs python3 -I tools/sort-youtube-watch-later-into-playlists/do-work/read_channel.py < request.json from the Workshop checkout.

4. Read the last printed JSON line: {"result":{"channels":[...]}} gives each channel's counts; {"error":...} says what to change. Keep the folder private, then run tool:plan-sorting-youtube-watch-later-into-playlists on it.

worked_examples.title: Read one channel's Watch Later, subscriptions and playlists
worked_examples.ask: Read my YouTube Watch Later and playlists for my kitchen channel.
worked_examples.given: From tools/sort-youtube-watch-later-into-playlists/test/test_sort.py (test_list_accounts_and_read_channel), with the signed-in account @a holding 1 Watch Later video, 1 subscription and 1 playlist titled Old. The AI runs, from the Workshop checkout: echo '{"cookies":"cookies.txt","out_dir":"yt-read","channels":[{"slug":"a","label":"A","sign_in_as":"@a"}]}' | python3 -I tools/sort-youtube-watch-later-into-playlists/do-work/read_channel.py
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"channels": [{"slug": "a", "watch_later": 1, "subscriptions": 1, "playlists": 1, "folder": "yt-read/a"}]}} and yt-read/a/ holds watch-later.json, subscriptions.json and playlists.json (playlists.json item title "Old").

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
